questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to Italy, and Milan was the only destination I could choose. But turned out amazing so glad I did.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best time! The only thing I missed was to get a broader international network, it became very easy to hang out with a lot of Danes. But it is definietly possible if you put energy in getting to know other people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There could be more information. But being a lot of Danish people we helped each other figure things out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: help from friends, a few mails and letters.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Spot A Home, I can really recommend. Then you know it is safe and legit and not a scam. You pay a little extra in adminstration fee but it is defenietly worth it. HousingAnywhere is the same.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I chose to live in an apartment with other flatmates which I loved. If you choose to live alone, just be aware that you really need to get yourself out there if you don't want to feel lonely. Some of my friends were surprised of this, because it is a new city and you don't have a network beforehand. So I would recommend living with someone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You change courses many times, and use a lot of time when you arrive to figure out a scheme that is possible. So don't stress about picking courses beforehand as these will defenietly change.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write to the mobility office in Milan, but I just used my friends and Unimi website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All the classes I applied for beforehand was not avaliable, but it was easy to get registrated at the courses I chose after.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't put too much energy beforehand in choosing courses, you will have to change them anyways.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was easier than at CPH but that was okay since I mostly came for the experience and not for academic development.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only had one course on the bachelor and 4 on the master. As a bachelor student you can still follow the Master courses just fine

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lectures, less discussion and more memorization. The exams was different from CPH, but in my courses everyone got a high score.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Narrating and Negotiating Identities, Digital Society, Languages of the Media, Understanding the Politics of Care and Value Change and Global Societies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked Narrating and Negotiating Identities and Understanding the Politics of Care as it was very interesting themes and content.
I only took Digital Society and Languages of the Media as the professor was American and the classes were very easy, so I had courses with low effort. In that way I could put more energy in the two other courses which were more interesting to me.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I expected to go out a lot for dinner and aperitifs, which I did, so nothing unexpected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to dinner and for aperitifs (aperols) were less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At our campus (La Statale) there was not any opportunities as I heard there was on some of the other campuses.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really any to my knowledge

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go to museums and markets - very cheap and good stuff

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to visit other citites, I was at Lake Como, Verona, Bergamo, Genova and to Rapallo to the ocean on a small vacation

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, drank coffee at the local café every morning, and got aperitifs in the evening

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I got to know the Italians by attending a class, and went to demonstrations with them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: they have a bit higher temper, so the traffic is very loud

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the ritualized coffee at the local cafe, the food, the aperols every afternoon, the markets, the fresh groceries, hearing the beautiful language everyday

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the Italian lifestyle, it is amazing 
Save some money so you feel free to spend it on restaurants, drinks, coffee and markets 
go on day-trips or small vacations

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't stress about the fact that the classes is very different, you get used to it and it will all work out at the end. I did not use many hours on studying and I got very high grades

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: just getting to know the great city with many different areas, getting amazing friends and living the Italian lifestyle

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: all the practical stuff, it takes a lot of time figuring out which courses to attend, and how the exams work but just go with the flow, everyone is a bit confused:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it! It has been the best!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
